Class ZipReader

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.build.ZipReader
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
public final class ZipReader extends Object implements Closeable
A read-only view of an existing .jar or .zip file, parsed by hand rather than through ZipFile.

The packaging library needs two things the JDK does not give it. First, the exact offset of every entry's first data byte, because the runner jar format indexes entry data by absolute offset and the launcher reads it with no ZIP parsing at all; that offset is only knowable by reading each local file header, whose name and extra field lengths may differ from the central directory record's. Second, the central directory order, which must be preserved into the runner jar so that JarFile.entries() over a nested jar reports the original order.

ZIP64 is handled explicitly: the end of central directory record is located by scanning back from the end of the file, the ZIP64 end of central directory record is read whenever a locator precedes it or any count, size or offset carries the IndexFormat.ZIP64_MARKER value, and the ZIP64 extended information extra field is parsed for every central directory record that needs it.

Entry names are decoded as UTF-8 regardless of the general purpose bit flag, which is what ZipFile does by default and what every jar in practice contains. Names that are unsafe to extract or to use as logical names are rejected while the archive is being read, so that no later stage of the pipeline has to remember to check (see isSafeEntryName(String)).

Instances hold an open file channel and must be closed. They are not thread-safe.

Since:
1.0

    • isSafeEntryName

      public static boolean isSafeEntryName(String name)
      Whether a name is safe to use as an entry name, both for extraction to a directory and as a logical name in the index.

      Rejected are: the empty name, names starting with '/' (absolute), Windows drive-letter prefixes such as C:/, names containing a backslash or a NUL character, empty path segments (a//b) and any . or .. segment. A single trailing '/', which marks a directory entry, is allowed.

      Parameters:
      name - the candidate entry name
      Returns:
      true when the name is safe

    • requireSafeEntryName

      public static void requireSafeEntryName(String name, String archive) throws IOException
      Checks an entry name with isSafeEntryName(String) and fails with a message naming both the archive and the offending entry.
      Parameters:
      name - the candidate entry name
      archive - a description of the archive the name came from, used in the error message
      Throws:
      IOException - if the name is not safe

    • isSignatureFile

      public static boolean isSignatureFile(String name)
      Whether an entry name is a jar signature file, which the packager drops because the runner jar is repacked and its nested jars can no longer be verified.

      The jar specification treats these names case-insensitively, so this check does too. The manifest itself is deliberately not included: per-jar manifests are kept verbatim.

      Parameters:
      name - the entry name
      Returns:
      true for META-INF/*.SF, *.DSA, *.RSA, *.EC and META-INF/SIG-*

    • isIndexList

      public static boolean isIndexList(String name)
      Whether an entry name is the jar index the packager drops, matched case-insensitively for the same reason signature files are.
      Parameters:
      name - the entry name
      Returns:
      true for META-INF/INDEX.LIST

      public List<ZipEntryInfo> entries()

    • manifest

      public Optional<Manifest> manifest()
      The archive's manifest, parsed once when the reader was opened.

      The manifest entry is looked up case-insensitively, as JarFile does. The returned object is the reader's own instance and is mutable; callers must not modify it.

      Returns:
      the manifest, or empty when the archive has no META-INF/MANIFEST.MF
